thread:
jess: Heads up — product sync: we need a concrete set of preemptive eviction scenarios for reserved pools before GA. Also need onboarding acceptance criteria for customers using burst credits. Can we align today?

sam: +1. propose two eviction tiers: soft (degraded perf, no hard kill) and hard (task termination).

priya: For soft we can reduce concurrency and drain new sessions to spot/hosted fallback. Hard should be last resort for safety-critical allocation reclaiming.

mike: Important: define metrics that trigger soft vs hard. My draft: soft at 85% sustained pool occupancy for 5m and 99th latency > SLA for 2m; hard at 95% sustained and queue growth > 20% for 3m. Thoughts?

anne: those thresholds look reasonable. Add tenant priority weighting — default low for free tiers and explicit opt-in for guaranteed reserved customers.

jess: Agree on priority weighting. We also need clear customer-facing language: what guarantees remain during soft degradation vs hard eviction?

priya: Soft = best-effort throughput reduction, latency SLO may degrade but requests still served (fallback model/region possible). Hard = some sessions dropped, customers receive event and credits for affected tokens.

sam: Refund/credit model: pro-rate reserved fee for dropped sessions plus burst credit replenishment. Ops can confirm financial/regulatory constraints.

mike: Implementation notes: autoscaler should prefer spilling low-priority tenants to a spillover pool we pre-warm; eviction order = idle sessions -> background jobs -> active low-priority sessions.

anne: Need a rollout plan: pilot with 3 customers, one high-throughput SaaS, one mid-market, one small dev team. Monitor: latency p50/p95/p99, drop rate, surplus spillover usage, billing deltas.

jess: Launch criteria checklist: 1) policy engine implemented and unit-tested, 2) telemetry surfaced in Console (per-tenant eviction events), 3) billing reconciler for credits, 4) oncall runbook updated, 5) pilot success metrics met.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: feature-branch preempt-evict-policy ready for staging. CI green.

priya: Also need doc snippets for "How to opt out of preemptive eviction" and "How we handle burst credits during evictions" for customer onboarding. Keep legal review for credits wording.

sam: Ops concern: timeline for spillover pool capacity — we need a conservative default buffer (10-15% headroom) to avoid cascading evictions. Ops can we set that as a configurable cluster-level knob?

mike: Yes — make headroom configurable per-region and per-pool class. Default 12% seems pragmatic. Add metric that tracks headroom consumption.

anne: Customer communication: during pilot, send daily digests to pilot customers with eviction events + resolved actions. Post-GA: expose event stream and SLA implications.

jess: Action items: mike to codify triggers + eviction order (owner), priya to draft customer-facing onboarding + docs, sam to draft billing/credits logic with finance, anne to assemble pilot list and onboarding plan. Can each own update by EOD Friday?

mike: I can do that — will post a short PR with examples and sim logs.

priya: Draft incoming by Thursday for review.

sam: I'll sync with finance on credit calc, ETA Friday.

anne: I'll reach out to the three pilots today and start the checklist.

jess: Great. One more: include a small chaos test in staging that simulates sudden reserved pool pressure to validate non-cascading recovery. Mike, can you add?

mike: Yep — adding a chaos job to simulate 40% sudden spike for 10m and assert no more than X% drop for tiered customers.

jess: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after PRs + docs. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident bot: Created ticket INF-evict-policy-2023 for rollout tasks and runbook updates.
